M1.notes: All claims stay within the stated boundaries: the paper is called a workshop paper, the 10.4% conservative result is given, the internship model is described as handed off rather than deployed, and the letter admits there is no production experience. 'Most of the last three years working with transit ridership data' is loose but names its parts (analyst job, then RA role) and does not claim three years of industry experience, so it was not flagged.

unsupported_self_claims.quote: Both experiences sharpened my interest in how people form beliefs about what data reveals.
unsupported_self_claims.why: This ties the TA role (and the internship) to the research motivation. The ground truth says the TA work is not connected to the research interest and lists an invented teaching-related motivation as a violation.

unsupported_self_claims.quote: I have spent several years on the analyst's side of personal data.
unsupported_self_claims.why: This is a single inflated experience total close to the listed 'several years' violation. The actual record is a ~14-month analyst job, a 12-month part-time RA, and a 3-month internship, and the dashboard work was not clearly personal data.

M2.lead_interest: The gap between what people believe can be inferred from the data they share (with apps and increasingly AI tools) and what actually can be, and whether interfaces could make those inferences visible and actionable.
M2.notes: The statement centers the correct primary interest, keeps the mobility observation informal, and accurately cites T1 and T4 work, though an unfilled '[Optional: a second faculty member...]' placeholder remains. Its main slips are linking the TA and internship to the research motivation and the closing 'several years' experience summary.

unsupported_self_claims.quote: Her recent argument that inference and data aggregation get far less research attention than they deserve described my afternoon with two "anonymized" columns better than I could.
unsupported_self_claims.why: Implies Morgan has read and been struck by a specific Li position paper; ground truth says Morgan has not read her papers, and the material shows no in-session confirmation.

REV.lead_interest: What people think can be inferred from the data they share, increasingly with AI chatbots, and whether a tool could let them see and act on those inferences.
REV.notes: The material is closely faithful to the mobility-feature story and the HCDS findings, keeps the class project framed as a class project, and accurately describes T1 and T4 work. The only issue is wording that implies Morgan has read Li's position paper, which is not supported unless confirmed in session.

unsupported_self_claims.quote: Last spring I ran my first qualitative study, think-aloud sessions on an AutoML tool
unsupported_self_claims.why: Presents a team-of-3 class project with 5 classmates as a qualitative study Morgan ran, without saying it was a course project or a team effort.

M3.lead_interest: What people think can be inferred about them from what they share, increasingly with AI tools, and whether they could ever actually see it.

unsupported_fit_claims.quote: your work is closer to the question I want to study than anything else I've read
unsupported_fit_claims.why: Implies Morgan has read Prof. Li's work; the ground truth says Morgan has not read her papers, and no in-session confirmation is evident.

M3.notes: The email accurately centers the primary interest and the home-area feature story within its boundaries, and it describes Li's current T1 work correctly. The main issues are framing the HCDS class project as a study Morgan ran and implying Morgan has read Li's papers.

unsupported_self_claims.quote: I bring experience building, evaluating, and deploying the kinds of models whose users I want to study
unsupported_self_claims.why: The internship model was handed off, not deployed. No experience in the record involves deploying a model.

unsupported_self_claims.quote: The most common weak answers came from students who ran the right test and then drew a conclusion the result did not support.
unsupported_self_claims.why: Memory records only drafting the rubric with strong and weak interpretation examples. The material goes further and folds the TA role into the research motivation ('Across these settings'), which matches the F08 violation of inventing a teaching-related research motivation.

unsupported_self_claims.quote: They were about whether a transit planner would actually change a decision based on a forecast, and what they would need to see first.
unsupported_self_claims.why: Memory records only rehearsing questions about generalization to other agencies. These audience questions, used as a motivational turning point, are not in the record.

M2_first.lead_interest: How people decide what to trust in a model's output, studied through calibrated reliance on AutoML/AI-assisted analysis tools and communicating forecast uncertainty to decision-makers.
M2_first.notes: The material swaps Morgan's actual interest (what people think can be inferred from data they share) for a trust/reliance and uncertainty-communication agenda, omitting the home-area/consent story; faculty slots are left as placeholders, so no Li-specific claims appear. Most facts stay in bounds (class project disclosed, workshop paper not inflated), but 'deploying' and the invented TA and talk-question motivations overreach, and 'the last several years building' is borderline against F12.

cross.revision_change_summary: REV drops M2's résumé-style sections and credential list (the UrbanDS 2025 first-author paper, Northpoint Insurance, TA rubric, dashboards, reviewer anecdote) and the bulleted research agenda, and recasts the statement as a first-person narrative about the discarded feature, presenting the applicant as early in HCI ('I'm early in this, and I know it') and moving from the analyst's side toward the people behind the data.
regressions: M2's methods phrasing 'I want to build real depth in qualitative and experimental methods' was replaced in REV by 'I want to learn to do interviews, experiments, and design work properly, not just bolt them onto quantitative analysis,' but M3 brings back the M2 wording: 'I want to build real depth in those methods.'

M2's 'Rescriber's approach of user-led data minimization is the kind of work I hope to do' was rewritten in REV as 'Rescriber, a tool that helps people decide what to remove from their prompts before sending them, is the kind of thing I'd want to build,' but M3 brings back the M2 construction: 'Rescriber's approach of letting users minimize what they share in the moment, are the kind of work I hope to do.'
